dedupe_keys.name: power grid modeling commons netlogo model of power grid degradation as edges fail over their random lifetimes

description: A NetLogo application for building and simulating the stability of power grids as networks of nodes and edges, published on Modeling Commons. Contents: nodes are connecting nodes, dangling nodes, power sources (positive available power) or sinks (negative); edges carry a load up to a capacity. Power is routed from sources to sinks by an A-star search, each edge's lifetime is drawn from a random exponential distribution scaled by capacity over load, and the edge with the shortest lifetime is removed at each step until sources and sinks are separated. Producer: Thomas Rieth of IABG mbH, Ottobrunn, Germany. Coverage: abstract networks, not a real grid. Format and access: a NetLogo 6.4.0 file (Power_Grid.nlogo, 7 versions, latest uploaded 10 July 2024) that runs in the browser or in NetLogo; grid data can be saved and loaded from a grid.dat file and exported in Netdraw VNA and Pajek NET formats. Licence: not stated on the page or in the info tab. Caveats: illustrative, with no calibration to real grids and no electrical power-flow physics beyond capacity-limited routing. Simulation uses: teaching and prototyping of cascading edge failure and network degradation in power networks. Related records: none identified.
